I am now applying for PIP after being diagnosed with ADHD, so I have been going through my medical records.

I went through appointment after appointment regarding my mental health as a teen, adolescent, and all the way up until I left to sign on with a new GP when I was at university. They consistently failed me every step of the way, not arguing my case, pushing me onto SSRIs which did nothing, and telling me that meds would be better than therapy as therapy would take 8 months to receive. The actual therapy from Havering IAPT was poor.

When I first went there, David Doyle was not keen to refer me to CAMH services, suggesting my anger, consistent low mood, and lack of pleasure was just "typical teenage behaviour", telling my mum she didn't need to worry. My GP didn't fight my case, and 6years later, my depression and anxiety got worse until I got useful help from my university's GP practice and took it upon myself to go and get help.

During all of this, multiple specialists and GPs saw me, including a paediatrician, and none of them even suspected I had ADHD. The clinician who diagnosed me said that the signs in childhood and teen years were clear. How all of the GPs, specalists, therapists etc didn't have an inkling I dont know.

Not all of this is the practice's fault, but I have to say they didn't fight my case, and wanted to offer me the easy route out of medication (I was 16 at the time and was pressured into SSRIs).

I have no clue how the practice is now, but like others have said, since Dr Bland left, this place went downhill. If you are in Romford/Hornchurch, find a GP practice who takes you and your children's mental health seriously.
